Diagrams (4)

  • Mermaid Diagram Renderer (lite)Renders a practical Mermaid subset to SVG, fully offline with a hand-written layered layout. Supported: flowchart/graph (TD TB LR RL BT; shapes [] () ([ ]) [[ ]] [( )] (( )) {} {{ }} [/ /]; edges --> --- -.-> ==> with |label| or -- text -->; chains A-->B-->C; & fan-out; subgraph...end (nested, edges into subgraphs); classDef/class/:::/style/linkStyle), sequenceDiagram (participant/actor aliases, ->> -->> -> --> -x -), +/- activations, notes, loop/alt/else/opt/par/and/critical/break/rect blocks, autonumber), pie (title, showData), gantt (sections, YYYY-MM-DD, durations d/w/h, after id, done/active/crit/milestone), erDiagram (entities with attributes, cardinalities, labels), stateDiagram-v2 (transitions, [*], composite states, choice/fork, notes, descriptions) and classDiagram (members, <<annotations>>, inheritance/composition/aggregation/association/dependency/realization, cardinalities). Not supported: themes/init directives, click/links, icons, markdown/KaTeX text, WITH-style styling beyond basics, mindmap/timeline/journey/git/quadrant/C4/etc. Text widths are estimated, so very tight labels can differ slightly from a browser render.
  • Graphviz DOT Renderer (lite)Renders a simple DOT subset to SVG offline with the built-in layered layout (not the real Graphviz engine, so positions differ). Supported: digraph/graph, rankdir, node/edge/graph default attributes, node and edge statements with chains and {a b} sets, quoted ids, label (with \n), shape (box ellipse circle diamond hexagon cylinder plaintext parallelogram), style (filled dashed dotted bold invis), color/fillcolor/fontcolor, arrowhead/arrowtail/dir, headlabel/taillabel, cluster subgraphs. Not supported: HTML labels, record ports, ports/compass points, splines/ratio/size/nodesep and other layout attributes (ignored).
  • SQL DDL to ER DiagramPaste CREATE TABLE statements (columns, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES, inline REFERENCES, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY) and get an entity-relationship diagram as SVG with crow's-foot notation. Generic SQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite syntax work; other statements are ignored.
  • Text to Mermaid Flowchart (Arrows, Outlines and Numbered Steps)Turn plain text into Mermaid diagram code: "A -> B -> C" chains, "Decision? yes: X / no: Y" branches, indented outlines (mind map) or numbered steps. A small syntax converter, not an AI.

SQL & Data (5)

  • SQL on CSV / JSON (in-browser SQL)Run SQL against pasted CSV or JSON. Box 1: tables separated by a line of ---, each CSV (first row = header) or a JSON array of objects, optionally starting with "-- name: users"; they become t1, t2, ... (and the name). You can also put CREATE TABLE / INSERT statements in either box. Box 2: statements separated by ;. Supported: SELECT with expressions, aliases, DISTINCT, WHERE (AND OR NOT, comparisons, LIKE, GLOB, IN, BETWEEN, IS [NOT] NULL, EXISTS), INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/CROSS JOIN with ON or USING, GROUP BY/HAVING, COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX TOTAL GROUP_CONCAT (DISTINCT ok), ORDER BY (aliases, ordinals, NULLS FIRST/LAST), LIMIT/OFFSET, subqueries (FROM, IN, EXISTS, scalar, correlated), WITH (non-recursive), UNION [ALL]/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, CASE, CAST, string and math functions, CREATE TABLE [AS], CREATE VIEW, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP. Differences from SQLite: "/" is always true division, numeric-looking text compares as a number, empty CSV cells are NULL, no constraint enforcement (PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE/NOT NULL), no window functions, recursive CTEs, triggers or date functions. Output is a text table plus CSV; nothing leaves your browser.
  • SQL INSERT to JSONParse INSERT ... VALUES statements (multi-row, quoted strings, NULL, booleans, numbers) into JSON rows per table. Column names come from the INSERT or the CREATE TABLE in the same script. Subset: INSERT/CREATE TABLE only; expressions stay as raw text.
  • SQL CREATE TABLE to TypeScriptTurn CREATE TABLE statements (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite flavours) into TypeScript interfaces: NOT NULL columns become required, nullable ones get "| null". Handles quoted identifiers, constraints and IF NOT EXISTS.
  • SQL Stored Procedure / CRUD GeneratorFrom a CREATE TABLE statement, generate CRUD stored routines for PostgreSQL (functions), MySQL (procedures) or SQL Server (T-SQL procedures): create, get by key, list, update, delete.
  • SQL INSERT to CSV ConverterParse INSERT ... VALUES statements into CSV. Column names become the header, multi-row inserts become rows, and NULL can be written as empty or as the word NULL.

Images – Extra (2)

  • HEIC to JPG / PNG / WebPConverts HEIC/HEIF photos using the browser's own image decoder, so it only works where the browser can already decode HEIC: Safari (macOS, iOS), and some Chrome/Edge builds on Windows or macOS that have the system HEVC/HEIF codecs installed. Firefox and most other setups cannot, and the tool will say so; there is no bundled software HEVC decoder (that cannot sensibly be hand-written). Files never leave your browser.
  • HEIC / HEIF Decoder (any browser)Decodes HEIC/HEIF photos (iPhone, Samsung, ...) with a built-in software HEVC decoder, so it works in every browser, including Chrome, Edge and Firefox without any codec; nothing is uploaded. Handles tiled (grid) photos and rotation/mirror/crop properties, and exports JPEG, PNG or WebP. Supported: still-image HEVC (intra / Main, Main Still Picture, Main 10 and 4:0:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4 up to 12 bit), multi-slice, tiles, wavefront, scaling lists, SAO and deblocking. Not supported: HEIC sequences/live-photo motion (only the primary still is decoded), overlay (iovl) images, alpha and depth maps, AVIF, ICC/Display-P3 colour management (pixel values are shown as stored). Large photos take a few seconds to decode on the CPU.

  • System Prompt XML BuilderTurn a plain outline of prompt sections into a well-structured, XML-tagged system prompt (the structure recommended for Claude and also effective for other models): role, context, instructions, constraints, examples (grouped in <examples>), output format and a document/input placeholder, with consistent tag names, escaped content where needed and an approximate token count.
  • LangGraph State & Graph GeneratorDescribe a LangGraph workflow in a few lines (state fields, nodes, edges, conditional routes) and get runnable Python: a TypedDict state with reducers (add_messages, operator.add), node function stubs, a StateGraph with edges and conditional edges, compile() and an invoke example.
  • OpenAI Chat Messages <-> Vercel AI SDK CoreMessage ConverterConvert a messages array between the OpenAI Chat Completions format and Vercel AI SDK CoreMessage / ModelMessage: string and multi-part content, image_url <-> image parts, assistant tool_calls <-> tool-call parts, tool role results <-> tool-result parts.   • Embedding Cost CalculatorEstimate the cost of embedding a corpus: documents x average tokens (or characters / words), re-embedding runs, and vector storage size (dimensions x 4 bytes, plus HNSW overhead estimate). Prices are list prices per 1M tokens at the time of writing and change often: override with "Custom price" and check your provider. Token counts from characters are an approximation (about 4 characters per English token).
  • Tiktoken Tokenizer Visualizer (cl100k / o200k)Exact OpenAI BPE tokenization (cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, embeddings v2/v3), o200k_base (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o1/o3 families)) shown as coloured tokens plus a table of ids and bytes. Runs offline in your browser. Only OpenAI encodings (cl100k_base, o200k_base) are included. Claude, DeepSeek and Gemini tokenizers are NOT included (their vocabularies are not available offline): use the llm-token-estimator tool for approximate counts of those.
  • GPT Token Counter (cl100k + o200k, chat overhead)Exact token counts for text under cl100k_base and o200k_base side by side, plus an approximate chat-message overhead calculator (OpenAI cookbook rule: 3 tokens per message, +1 per name, +3 reply priming; use o200k_base for the GPT-4o family). Only OpenAI encodings (cl100k_base, o200k_base) are included. Claude, DeepSeek and Gemini tokenizers are NOT included (their vocabularies are not available offline): use the llm-token-estimator tool for approximate counts of those.
  • Token ID Decoder / Encoder (tiktoken)Convert token ids to text and text to token ids with exact cl100k_base / o200k_base vocabularies. Only OpenAI encodings (cl100k_base, o200k_base) are included. Claude, DeepSeek and Gemini tokenizers are NOT included (their vocabularies are not available offline): use the llm-token-estimator tool for approximate counts of those.
  • Token Cost Estimator (your own prices)Exact token count (cl100k_base / o200k_base) multiplied by prices YOU enter per 1M tokens. No prices are built in: copy the current figures from your provider's pricing page. Only OpenAI encodings (cl100k_base, o200k_base) are included. Claude, DeepSeek and Gemini tokenizers are NOT included (their vocabularies are not available offline): use the llm-token-estimator tool for approximate counts of those.
  • Truncate / Chunk Text by Tokens (tiktoken)Cut text to at most N tokens, or split it into chunks of at most N tokens with overlap, always on a token boundary that does not split a UTF-8 character. Exact cl100k_base / o200k_base. Only OpenAI encodings (cl100k_base, o200k_base) are included. Claude, DeepSeek and Gemini tokenizers are NOT included (their vocabularies are not available offline): use the llm-token-estimator tool for approximate counts of those.
  • Multi-Tokenizer Token Counter (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, ...)Count the tokens of one text under every included tokenizer at once, sorted from fewest to most: gpt2 (GPT-2; identical ranks to r50k_base); r50k_base (GPT-3 davinci/curie/babbage/ada); p50k_base (text-davinci-002/003, Codex); cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo); o200k_base (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o1/o3); DeepSeek-V3 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3); DeepSeek-R1 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1); Qwen2.5 (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B); Phi-4 (microsoft/phi-4); GPT-NeoX-20B (Pythia, EleutherAI); StarCoder2 (bigcode/starcoder2); Mistral-7B-v0.3 (mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.3); claude-legacy (LEGACY Claude 1/2 only, NOT Claude 3/4/5). Exact vocabularies, runs offline in your browser (vocabularies load on first use, about 20 MB in total). Exact for the listed models; LEGACY Claude 1/2 tokenizer (from the public npm package @anthropic-ai/tokenizer). It is NOT accurate for Claude 3, 4 or 5-family models: Anthropic has not published those vocabularies. Gemini, Llama, Gemma and Claude 3+ tokenizers are not included (gated or unpublished).
  • Tokenizer Visualizer (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, GPT-2, Claude legacy ...)Pick an encoding and see the text as coloured tokens plus a table of ids and bytes. Encodings: gpt2 (GPT-2; identical ranks to r50k_base); r50k_base (GPT-3 davinci/curie/babbage/ada); p50k_base (text-davinci-002/003, Codex); cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo); o200k_base (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o1/o3); DeepSeek-V3 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3); DeepSeek-R1 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1); Qwen2.5 (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B); Phi-4 (microsoft/phi-4); GPT-NeoX-20B (Pythia, EleutherAI); StarCoder2 (bigcode/starcoder2); Mistral-7B-v0.3 (mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.3); claude-legacy (LEGACY Claude 1/2 only, NOT Claude 3/4/5). Exact for the listed models; LEGACY Claude 1/2 tokenizer (from the public npm package @anthropic-ai/tokenizer). It is NOT accurate for Claude 3, 4 or 5-family models: Anthropic has not published those vocabularies. Gemini, Llama, Gemma and Claude 3+ tokenizers are not included (gated or unpublished).
  • Token IDs <-> Text (all encodings)Convert token ids to text and text to token ids with any included encoding: gpt2 (GPT-2; identical ranks to r50k_base); r50k_base (GPT-3 davinci/curie/babbage/ada); p50k_base (text-davinci-002/003, Codex); cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo); o200k_base (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o1/o3); DeepSeek-V3 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3); DeepSeek-R1 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1); Qwen2.5 (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B); Phi-4 (microsoft/phi-4); GPT-NeoX-20B (Pythia, EleutherAI); StarCoder2 (bigcode/starcoder2); Mistral-7B-v0.3 (mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.3); claude-legacy (LEGACY Claude 1/2 only, NOT Claude 3/4/5). Exact for the listed models; LEGACY Claude 1/2 tokenizer (from the public npm package @anthropic-ai/tokenizer). It is NOT accurate for Claude 3, 4 or 5-family models: Anthropic has not published those vocabularies. Gemini, Llama, Gemma and Claude 3+ tokenizers are not included (gated or unpublished).
  • JSON to TOON Converter (Token-Oriented Object Notation)Convert JSON to TOON, the compact indentation format with tabular arrays that uses fewer LLM tokens. Shows the saving.
  • TOON to JSON ConverterDecode TOON (indented objects, inline and tabular arrays, list items) back to JSON, with line-numbered errors.
  • Prompt Injection Scanner (Untrusted Text Check)Scan web pages, emails, PDFs or user input that will be fed to an LLM for prompt-injection signs: instruction overrides, fake system tags, exfiltration links, hidden Unicode. Pattern based, nothing sent anywhere.
  • Prompt Compressor (Cut Filler, Save Tokens)Shorten a prompt or system message by removing politeness filler, wordy phrases, duplicate lines and extra whitespace, and show the estimated token saving and each change. Rule based.
  • Needle-in-a-Haystack Test Text GeneratorBuild a long filler document with one "needle" sentence hidden at a chosen depth, to test an LLM's long-context recall. Deterministic with a seed, with a question and expected answer.
  • LLM Logprobs Analyzer (Token Confidence, Perplexity, Uncertain Spans)Paste the logprobs from an OpenAI-style API response and see per-token probability, perplexity, entropy from top alternatives, and the low-confidence spans where the model was unsure. Runs locally.
  • Agent Context Window Simulator (What Survives Truncation)Paste a chat or agent message list and see which messages stay in a limited context window under different strategies: drop oldest, keep system plus recent, or keep pinned messages. Shows token use per message.

AI & LLM (12)

  • Few-Shot Prompt FormatterFormat input => output example pairs as a few-shot prompt: plain labels, XML tags, Markdown, or ready-to-send OpenAI / Anthropic message JSON. Use \n inside an example for line breaks.
  • Chain-of-Thought Prompt BuilderWrap a task in a reasoning prompt pattern: zero-shot CoT, structured steps, plan-and-solve, self-consistency, step-back, tree-of-thought panel or scratchpad tags, with a choice of answer format.
  • LLM Context Window ShrinkerShrink text to fit a token budget: keep head, tail, both ends, drop duplicate lines, or keep the most informative sentences in original order (frequency-based extractive summary). Token counts are estimates (characters / ratio), not a real tokenizer.
  • Embedding Token & Cost EstimatorEstimate tokens, chunk count, API cost and vector storage for embedding your corpus across popular embedding models. Token counts are estimates (characters / ratio) and the price table is a built-in snapshot: override it with your own price.
  • AI Fill-Mask: Predict the Missing Word (DistilBERT)Put [MASK] in an English sentence and a DistilBERT language model, running in your browser, ranks the most likely words. No upload, no API.
  • AI Question Answering from a Passage (DistilBERT SQuAD)Paste a passage and ask a question: a DistilBERT model fine-tuned on SQuAD finds the answer span in the text, entirely in your browser.
  • AI Language Identifier (fastText, 176 Languages)Identify the language of any text with Facebook's fastText lid.176 model (917 KB), run by a JavaScript port in your browser. Shows probabilities and can check every line.
  • AI Image Classifier (MobileNetV2, 1000 ImageNet Classes)Drop in a photo and a small neural network (MobileNetV2) running in your browser names what it shows from 1000 everyday object classes, with probabilities. The image never leaves your device.
  • AI Speech to Text (Whisper tiny, English, Offline in Your Browser)Transcribe an audio file or your microphone to English text with OpenAI Whisper tiny running in your browser. 43 MB model downloaded once; your audio is never uploaded. Slow but private.
  • Offline AI Chat (SmolLM2 135M, Private, Runs in Your Browser)Chat with a small open language model (SmolLM2-135M-Instruct) that runs entirely in your browser tab. 76 MB download once, no account, no server, no logging. A tiny model: good for demos and simple questions, not for facts.
  • Train Your Own Text Classifier (Naive Bayes, In Your Browser)Paste labelled examples ("label: text") and texts to classify. A multinomial Naive Bayes model trains instantly in your browser and predicts labels with probabilities, top clue words and a leave-one-out accuracy estimate.
  • Auto Caption Generator: SRT and VTT from Speech (Whisper in Your Browser)Turn the speech in an audio or video file into timed SRT or WebVTT captions with the Whisper tiny English model running in your browser. Edit the text, then download. English only, slow, private.

Schema Converters (24)

  • TypeScript Interface to JSON SchemaConvert TypeScript interfaces, type aliases and enums to JSON Schema draft-07 (definitions + $ref). Supports optional props, unions, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, index signatures, extends/intersections and JSDoc descriptions. Not supported: conditional/mapped types, keyof/typeof and most utility generics.
  • TypeScript Interface to Zod SchemaConvert TypeScript interfaces, type aliases and enums into Zod schemas (z.object, z.enum, z.union, z.tuple, z.record, optional/nullable, descriptions from JSDoc) plus inferred types. Same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool.
  • Zod Schema to TypeScript TypeStatically convert Zod schema source (z.object, z.string().min(), z.enum, z.union, z.array, z.record, optional/nullable/nullish, extend/merge, describe) into the equivalent TypeScript types, i.e. what z.infer would produce. The code is parsed, never executed. .transform() outputs and custom refinements are not inferable.
  • YAML to TypeScript InterfacesInfer TypeScript interfaces from YAML (or JSON) data: nested objects become named interfaces, arrays of objects are merged so missing keys become optional, mixed values become unions. Multi-document YAML: first document is used.
  • JSON to Pydantic ModelsGenerate Pydantic v2 BaseModel classes from sample JSON: nested classes, List/Optional/Union typing, datetime/date/UUID detection, snake_case attributes with Field(alias=...) when the JSON key is camelCase or a Python keyword. Arrays of objects are merged to find optional fields.
  • JSON to TypeScript Type GuardsFrom sample JSON, generate TypeScript interfaces plus runtime type-guard functions (isRoot(value): value is Root) that check every property, nested object, array element, optional and nullable field. Handy for validating API responses without a schema library.
  • GraphQL Schema to TypeScriptConvert GraphQL SDL (type, input, interface, enum, union, scalar, descriptions) into TypeScript interfaces and types. Interface fields are inlined into implementing types; nullable output fields become "T | null", nullable input fields become optional. Query/Mutation root types are skipped unless enabled; field arguments are ignored.
  • GraphQL Schema to ZodConvert GraphQL SDL types, inputs, enums and unions into Zod schemas (z.object, z.enum, z.union, .nullable() / .optional(), z.array). Custom scalars map to z.string() (edit as needed). Recursive types use z.lazy.
  • Protobuf Message to Sample JSONParse a .proto (proto2/proto3) file and generate a sample JSON document for a message following the canonical proto3 JSON mapping: lowerCamelCase names, int64 as strings, bytes as base64, enums by name, maps as objects, Timestamp as RFC 3339, oneof (first member only).
  • Protobuf to TypeScript InterfacesConvert .proto messages and enums to TypeScript interfaces/types matching the proto3 JSON mapping (nested messages become Outer_Inner, repeated -> arrays, map -> Record, oneof members optional, int64 as string or number, Timestamp as string). Services are ignored.
  • Protobuf to JSON SchemaConvert .proto messages and enums to a JSON Schema draft-07 document with definitions, following the proto3 JSON mapping (int64 as numeric strings, bytes as base64, Timestamp as date-time).
  • JSON Schema to ProtobufConvert a JSON Schema (draft-07 / 2020-12 subset with properties, $ref/definitions, enums, arrays, additionalProperties) into proto3 messages: nested objects become messages, arrays become repeated, string enums get an UNSPECIFIED zero value, date-time maps to google.protobuf.Timestamp, non-required fields are optional. oneOf/anyOf with several non-null branches fall back to google.protobuf.Value.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to Python TypesConvert TypeScript interfaces, type aliases and enums into Python TypedDict, dataclass or Pydantic v2 models (str | None, list[...], Literal, tuple, datetime, nested models). Same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool.
  • MessagePack & CBOR Decoder / EncoderPaste MessagePack or CBOR bytes (hex or base64) to see them as JSON, or turn JSON into MessagePack / CBOR hex. Byte strings, tags and extension types are shown explicitly.
  • BSON Hex / Base64 to JSON (MongoDB Extended JSON) and BackDecode a BSON document from hex or base64 into MongoDB Extended JSON ($oid, $date, $numberLong, $binary), or encode such JSON to BSON bytes.
  • JSON Schema to TypeScriptGenerate TypeScript interfaces and types from a JSON Schema: required and optional properties, enums, const, oneOf / anyOf / allOf, arrays, tuples, $defs and $ref.
  • JSON to Protobuf (.proto) GeneratorInfer a proto3 schema from a JSON sample: nested messages, repeated fields, int32 / int64 / double / bool / string, with field numbers assigned in order.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to Go StructsConvert TypeScript interfaces and enums to Go structs with json tags: optional properties get omitempty (and pointers), nullable ones pointers, arrays become slices, Record becomes map[string]T, Date becomes time.Time, string enums become typed constants. Reads the same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool: interfaces, type aliases, string enums, optional and nullable properties, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, extends and intersections, JSDoc. Not supported: conditional and mapped types, keyof/typeof, function types, most utility generics.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to Rust Serde StructsConvert TypeScript interfaces and enums to Rust structs deriving Serialize and Deserialize: Option for optional and nullable fields, Vec, HashMap, tuples, serde rename or rename_all = "camelCase", Box on recursive fields, enums with per-variant renames. Reads the same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool: interfaces, type aliases, string enums, optional and nullable properties, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, extends and intersections, JSDoc. Not supported: conditional and mapped types, keyof/typeof, function types, most utility generics.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to Kotlin Data ClassesConvert TypeScript interfaces and enums to Kotlin data classes with nullable types and = null defaults, List and Map, enum classes, and optional kotlinx.serialization (@Serializable, @SerialName) or Jackson (@JsonProperty) annotations. Reads the same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool: interfaces, type aliases, string enums, optional and nullable properties, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, extends and intersections, JSDoc. Not supported: conditional and mapped types, keyof/typeof, function types, most utility generics.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to Java RecordsConvert TypeScript interfaces and enums to Java 17 records with List and Map, enums, boxed types for nullable fields and optional Jackson @JsonProperty annotations, wrapped in one public class so a single file compiles. Reads the same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool: interfaces, type aliases, string enums, optional and nullable properties, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, extends and intersections, JSDoc. Not supported: conditional and mapped types, keyof/typeof, function types, most utility generics.
  • TypeScript Interfaces to C# ClassesConvert TypeScript interfaces and enums to C# classes or records with nullable reference types, List and Dictionary, enums, and optional System.Text.Json ([JsonPropertyName]) or Newtonsoft.Json ([JsonProperty]) attributes. Reads the same TypeScript subset as the TypeScript to JSON Schema tool: interfaces, type aliases, string enums, optional and nullable properties, literals, tuples, arrays, Record, Date, extends and intersections, JSDoc. Not supported: conditional and mapped types, keyof/typeof, function types, most utility generics.
  • Python Classes to TypeScript InterfacesConvert Python TypedDict, dataclass, Pydantic v2 BaseModel, NamedTuple, Enum and plain annotated classes into TypeScript interfaces and types: Optional and X | None become | null, fields with defaults become optional, Literal becomes a literal union, list/set/dict/tuple/datetime/UUID are mapped, Pydantic aliases become the property names. Reads declarations only (a line-based parser, not a Python interpreter): no runtime-built models, validators or computed fields.
  • Go Structs to TypeScript InterfacesConvert Go struct definitions into TypeScript interfaces using their json tags: omitempty makes a property optional, pointers become | null, slices become arrays, map[string]T becomes Record, time.Time becomes string, embedded structs become extends, json:"-" and unexported fields are dropped, typed string and iota constants become enums or unions. Reads declarations only: custom MarshalJSON methods and build tags are not seen.

SQL Tools (18)

  • SQL DDL Converter (PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite)Convert CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX DDL between PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite: SERIAL <-> AUTO_INCREMENT, BOOLEAN <-> TINYINT(1), TIMESTAMPTZ <-> DATETIME, UUID <-> CHAR(36), JSONB <-> JSON, defaults (now(), true/false), identifier quoting, PK/UNIQUE/FK and indexes. DDL is parsed and re-emitted; views, triggers, functions, partitions and CHECK constraints are not carried over.
  • Prisma Schema to SQL DDLConvert a schema.prisma (models, enums, @id, @unique, @default, @map/@@map, @db.* types, @relation foreign keys, @@id/@@unique/@@index) into CREATE TABLE statements for PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite. Follows Prisma default type mappings (String -> text / varchar(191) on MySQL); client-side defaults such as uuid()/cuid() produce no SQL default.
  • SQL DDL to Prisma SchemaConvert CREATE TABLE statements (PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite syntax) to a schema.prisma: models with @id, @default(autoincrement()/now()), @unique, @map/@@map for snake_case columns, @db.* native types, composite @@id/@@unique/@@index, foreign keys as @relation with generated back-relation lists.
  • SQL DDL to Drizzle ORM SchemaConvert CREATE TABLE statements into a Drizzle ORM TypeScript schema for PostgreSQL (pg-core), MySQL (mysql-core) or SQLite (sqlite-core): column builders, primaryKey/notNull/unique/default/defaultNow, references() with onDelete, composite primary keys and indexes.
  • SQL DDL to Django ModelsConvert CREATE TABLE statements to Django models.py: field classes with max_length, decimal precision, null/blank, unique, defaults, ForeignKey(on_delete=...), db_table and db_column so the models map onto the existing tables. The implicit "id" AutoField is omitted; composite keys become unique_together (Django has no composite PKs).
  • SQL DDL to SQLAlchemy 2.0 ModelsConvert CREATE TABLE statements to SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models using Mapped[...] / mapped_column(): column types, nullable, unique, primary keys, ForeignKey with ondelete, server defaults, UniqueConstraint and Index in __table_args__. Relationship() attributes are not generated.
  • SQL DDL to Go GORM StructsConvert CREATE TABLE statements to Go GORM model structs: Go-style field names (ID, URL...), pointer types for nullable columns, gorm tags (column, primaryKey, autoIncrement, size, not null, uniqueIndex, default, precision), json tags, belongs-to association fields for foreign keys and TableName() methods.
  • SQL DDL to TypeORM / Sequelize ModelsConvert CREATE TABLE statements to TypeORM entity classes (decorators, ManyToOne + JoinColumn, Index/Unique) or Sequelize model definitions (DataTypes, associations). For Prisma, Drizzle, Django, SQLAlchemy and GORM use the dedicated converters.
  • SQL Keyword UppercaserUppercase (or lowercase) SQL keywords, and optionally built-in function names and data types, while leaving string literals, quoted identifiers, comments and your own table/column names untouched.
  • SQL Query Explainer (plain English)Explain a SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / CREATE TABLE statement in plain English: tables and joins, filters, grouping, ordering and limits in logical execution order, plus warnings about common pitfalls (SELECT *, leading-wildcard LIKE, functions on columns, big OFFSET, UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE). Rule-based parser: no CTEs, UNION or window frames.
  • SQL Index AdvisorPaste your CREATE TABLE statements and the SELECT / UPDATE / DELETE queries you run: get CREATE INDEX suggestions based on WHERE equality and range columns, join keys and ORDER BY / GROUP BY, skipping indexes already provided by primary keys, UNIQUE constraints or existing indexes. Static heuristic (no table statistics): always confirm with EXPLAIN on real data.
  • SQL to MongoDB QueryTranslate SQL into MongoDB shell syntax: SELECT -> find() with filter, projection, sort, skip, limit (or distinct); GROUP BY / aggregates / simple JOINs -> aggregate pipeline ($match, $lookup, $group, $project, $sort); INSERT VALUES -> insertOne/insertMany; UPDATE -> updateMany with $set/$inc; DELETE -> deleteMany. LIKE becomes a regex. Subqueries, UNION and CTEs are not supported.
  • MongoDB Query to SQLTranslate MongoDB shell queries to SQL: find/findOne with filters ($and, $or, $in, $gt..., $regex -> LIKE/REGEXP, $exists), projection, sort/skip/limit, countDocuments, distinct, insertOne/Many, updateOne/Many ($set, $inc, $unset), deleteOne/Many and simple aggregate pipelines ($match, $group, $sort, $limit, $project, $lookup). The query is parsed, never executed.
  • PostgreSQL EXPLAIN Plan VisualizerPaste EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE output (text or FORMAT JSON) and get an indented plan tree with per-node exclusive time or cost bars, row-estimate error factors and automatic findings: sequential scans that discard most rows, external (disk) sorts, multi-batch hashes, wildly wrong estimates, hot nested loops.
  • SQL Parameter Inliner (Fill ?, $1, :name Placeholders)Substitute bound parameters (?, $1, :name, @name, %s) into a SQL statement with correct literal escaping, to read or replay a logged query. For debugging, never for building queries.
  • SQL SELECT Query BuilderBuild a SELECT with columns, joins, filters, grouping, ordering and limit from simple lines of input, for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite or SQL Server, with identifiers quoted correctly.
  • SQL Migration Generator (Up / Down)Generate up and down migration SQL for common schema changes: create table, add column, drop column, rename, add index, add foreign key, for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.
  • MongoDB Query Builder (find, filter, sort, projection)Build a MongoDB find() or aggregate() command from simple conditions, with $and, $in, $regex, ranges, projection, sort and limit, as mongosh code and as JSON.

Mobile & Desktop Config (8)

  • AndroidManifest.xml BuilderGenerate an AndroidManifest.xml: package namespace, application attributes (label, icon, theme, allowBackup, cleartext traffic, backup rules), launcher activity with explicit android:exported, optional deep-link / App Link intent filter, permissions (short names like CAMERA are expanded to android.permission.*) with a list of those that need a runtime prompt, and optional hardware features.
  • iOS Info.plist BuilderGenerate an iOS Info.plist: bundle identifiers and versions, supported orientations, launch screen, usage-description strings (camera, photos, location, microphone, Face ID, tracking... via short aliases or full NS* keys), custom URL schemes, LSApplicationQueriesSchemes, background modes and App Transport Security exceptions. Output is valid XML property-list syntax.
  • Flutter Material 3 Theme GeneratorGenerate Dart code for a Material 3 ThemeData: light and dark themes from a seed colour via ColorScheme.fromSeed (the real tonal palette is computed by Flutter at runtime, this tool does not approximate it), font family, corner radius, app bar, filled/elevated button, input field and card styling, with optional explicit colour overrides.
  • Xcode Asset Catalog Contents.json GeneratorGenerate the Contents.json files of an .xcassets catalog: an App Icon set (modern single 1024 px icon with dark / tinted variants, or the full legacy iPhone + iPad size matrix with expected pixel dimensions), an Image set (1x / 2x / 3x, optional dark and template rendering) or a Color set (sRGB light + dark appearances). Includes the folder layout and file names to use.
  • Electron App Config Builder (secure defaults)Generate a secure-by-default Electron starter: main.js (BrowserWindow with contextIsolation, sandbox, no nodeIntegration, navigation and window-open blocking, Content-Security-Policy header, single-instance lock), a preload.js exposing a minimal IPC bridge, and package.json with an electron-builder configuration (appId, mac / win / linux targets, file globs).
  • Capacitor Config Builder (capacitor.config.ts / .json)Generate capacitor.config.ts or capacitor.config.json: appId, appName, webDir, server options (live-reload URL, cleartext, androidScheme), plugin settings for SplashScreen, StatusBar, Keyboard and PushNotifications, and iOS / Android specific options.
  • Universal Links / App Links Validator (AASA & assetlinks.json)Validate an apple-app-site-association file (iOS Universal Links: applinks.details with appIDs and components or legacy paths, webcredentials, appclips) or Android assetlinks.json (delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls, package_name, 32-byte SHA-256 fingerprints). Reports structural errors and warnings, and can test a URL path against the AASA rules. It checks the file content only: hosting (HTTPS, no redirects, /.well-known/, application/json) must be verified on your server.
  • Web App Manifest (PWA) GeneratorBuild manifest.webmanifest with name, icons, display mode, theme colors, shortcuts and the <link> tags, with installability checks.

Calculators (14)

  • Bitwise Calculator (AND, OR, XOR, shifts, rotate)Apply AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR, NOT, left / arithmetic right / logical right shifts, rotations, popcount, leading / trailing zeros and bit reversal to 8, 16, 32 or 64-bit values, with two's-complement signed or unsigned interpretation. Inputs accept decimal, 0x hex, 0b binary and 0o octal; results are shown in all four bases with the bit pattern.
  • Arbitrary-Precision Calculator (big integers & decimals)Evaluate expressions with unlimited-size integers and exact decimals: + - * / % ^ ** ! parentheses, sqrt, abs, gcd, lcm, powmod, floor, round, factorial, fib, pi and e. Add, subtract and multiply are exact; division and sqrt are rounded to the chosen number of decimal places. One expression per line.
  • Time Zone Meeting PlannerFind meeting times that work across time zones: list participants with IANA time zones (Europe/Brussels, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata...), pick a date and working hours, and see a half-hour grid of local times with DST applied for that date plus the best slots where everybody (or the most people) is within working hours.
  • Cron Time Zone ConverterConvert a 5-field cron expression written for one time zone into the equivalent in another (for example a job that must run at 09:00 Europe/Brussels on a UTC-only scheduler), shifting hours and, when the shift crosses midnight, the day-of-week / day-of-month fields. The offset is computed for the reference date you give, so the result is exact only on that side of a DST change: the tool says so.
  • Natural Language to CronTurn plain English schedules into a standard 5-field cron expression and read it back to confirm: "every 15 minutes", "every weekday at 8:30am", "every monday and friday at 5pm", "first day of every month at midnight", "every 2 hours between 9am and 5pm on weekdays", "quarterly", "on the 1st and 15th at noon". Rule-based (no AI), English only; unrecognised words are reported. One schedule per line.
  • Matrix Calculator (exact fractions)Add, subtract, multiply, transpose, determinant, inverse, rank, trace, RREF, matrix power and linear-system solving (A x = b) with exact rational arithmetic (BigInt fractions, so 1/3 stays 1/3), plus real eigenvalues via QR iteration (floating point, may not converge for complex eigenvalues). Entries: integers, decimals or fractions like 3/4, separated by spaces or commas, one row per line.
  • Statistics Calculator (Mean, SD, Variance, Quartiles, z-Score)Paste numbers and get count, sum, mean, median, mode, range, sample and population standard deviation and variance, quartiles, IQR, mean absolute deviation, outliers and z-scores.
  • Weighted Grade Calculator (and Final Exam Grade Needed)Enter assignments with scores and weights to get your current weighted grade, then see what you need on the remaining work to reach a target grade, and the letter grade.
  • Resistor Colour Code Calculator (4, 5, 6 Band & SMD)Decode resistor colour bands to ohms, tolerance and temperature coefficient, find the bands for a value, and read 3 or 4 digit SMD codes (103, 4R7, 01C).
  • UART Baud Rate Divisor & Error CalculatorFind the baud rate register value for a microcontroller clock (AVR UBRR, generic divisor), the actual baud rate and the percentage error, for 16x and 8x oversampling.
  • PWM Calculator (Duty Cycle, Frequency, Average Voltage)Convert between PWM frequency, period, duty cycle and on-time, and see the average voltage and timer counts for a given timer clock, prescaler and resolution.
  • Wavelength & Antenna Length CalculatorConvert radio frequency to wavelength and get half-wave dipole, quarter-wave monopole and full-wave lengths with a velocity factor, in metres, feet and inches.
  • Battery Life Estimator (Duty-Cycled IoT Device)Estimate battery life for a device that wakes, works and sleeps: average current from active and sleep currents and times, with a derating for self-discharge, temperature and ageing.
  • Birthday Paradox & Hash Collision Probability CalculatorProbability that at least two of n items collide in a space of N possibilities (birthdays, random IDs, truncated hashes), and how many items give a 50% or 1-in-a-million chance.

Markup Converters (16)

  • Markdown to BBCodeConvert Markdown to BBCode for forums (phpBB, vBulletin, XenForo...): headings -> [size][b], bold / italic / strikethrough, links, images, inline and fenced code -> [code], block quotes -> [quote], bullet and numbered lists -> [list][*], horizontal rules. Tables and raw HTML are passed through as text.
  • BBCode to MarkdownConvert forum BBCode to Markdown: [b] [i] [s] [u] (as HTML <u>), [url], [img], [quote], [code], [list] with [*] items (bullet or numbered), [size] / [color] / [center] wrappers (dropped, content kept) and [hr]. Unknown tags are left as-is.
  • JSX to HTML ConverterConvert static JSX into plain HTML: className -> class, htmlFor -> for, camelCase attributes, style={{ fontSize: 14 }} -> style="font-size:14px", {"text"} string expressions, self-closing tags expanded, fragments and {/* comments */} removed, event handlers / key / ref / spreads dropped. Dynamic expressions stay visible as {{ ... }} placeholders and are listed in a note, because JSX logic (map, ternaries, components) cannot be evaluated statically.
  • HTML Table Converter (CSV / TSV / Markdown / JSON / SQL)Extract <table> elements from HTML and convert them to CSV, TSV, Markdown table, JSON array of objects or SQL INSERT statements. Handles colspan / rowspan, nested tags, entities and <br>. Use the table number to pick one table when the page has several.
  • Markdown to Slides (HTML presentation)Turn Markdown into a slide deck: slides are separated by a line containing only ---, speaker notes start with "Note:". The preview scrolls slide by slide; the downloadable HTML file is fully self-contained (no network) with keyboard navigation (arrows, space, F for fullscreen, Home / End), a progress bar and print-to-PDF styles with one slide per page.
  • Property List (plist) to JSON and BackConvert Apple XML property lists (Info.plist, entitlements, preferences) to JSON and JSON to plist. Dates and binary data are kept as {"$date"} and {"$data"}.
  • HTML Validator: Unclosed Tags, Bad Nesting and Duplicate IDsPaste HTML and get a list with line numbers: unclosed or stray tags, block elements inside p, nested links, list and table structure, duplicate ids and attributes, obsolete tags and missing basics.
  • HTML to Pug Converter (Indented Template Syntax)Convert HTML markup into Pug (Jade) templates: tag names with #id and .class shorthand, attribute lists, piped text, comments, doctype and dot blocks for script and style.
  • HTML Sanitizer: Strip Scripts, Event Handlers and Unsafe URLsClean untrusted HTML with a strict allow-list: scripts, styles, forms, event handlers and javascript: URLs are removed, and every removal is listed with its line number.
  • HTML DOM Diff: Compare Two Pages by Elements, Attributes and TextCompare two HTML documents as trees, ignoring formatting and whitespace. See added, removed and changed elements, attributes and text with their element path.
  • Email HTML CSS Inliner (style Blocks to style Attributes)Move CSS rules from style blocks onto each matching element as inline style attributes for HTML email, keeping media queries and pseudo-class rules in a style block.
  • Responsive iframe Embed Code Builder (aspect-ratio, lazy, sandbox)Build iframe markup that scales to its container: aspect ratio, title, lazy loading, allowfullscreen, referrer policy and a sandbox preset, with a CSS fallback for old browsers.
  • BBCode to HTML Converter with Safe Links and PreviewConvert forum BBCode (b, i, u, s, url, img, quote, code, list, color, size, align) into HTML. Text is escaped, only http, https, mailto and ftp links are kept, and problems are listed.
  • MJML Subset Compiler: Responsive Email Markup to Table-Based HTMLCompile a practical subset of MJML (section, column, text, image, button, divider, spacer, head attributes) into responsive, table-based email HTML with a live preview.
  • LaTeX Math to MathML Converter with Live PreviewConvert LaTeX math (fractions, roots, sums, integrals, scripts, Greek, matrices, cases, left/right delimiters) into MathML that browsers typeset natively. Copy the MathML or paste it into HTML.
  • reStructuredText to HTML Converter (Common Subset, Offline)Render common reStructuredText to HTML in the browser: section titles, paragraphs, lists, literal blocks, code-block, admonitions, links and targets, with warnings that carry line numbers.

API Converters (5)

  • Postman Collection to OpenAPI 3Convert a Postman Collection (v2.0 / v2.1 JSON) into an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document: folders become tags, {{variables}} and :params become path parameters, query params and headers become parameters, JSON / urlencoded / form-data bodies become requestBody schemas inferred from the example, saved responses become response examples, bearer / basic / apikey auth becomes securitySchemes. Schemas are inferred from examples, so review required fields and types.
  • OpenAPI to Postman CollectionConvert an OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 document (JSON or YAML) into a Postman Collection v2.1: operations grouped into folders by tag, {{baseUrl}} variable from servers, path / query / header parameters, request bodies generated from examples or schemas, bearer / basic / API key auth at collection level.
  • HTTP Raw Message <-> JSON (wire format)Parse a raw HTTP/1.x request or response (start line, headers, body, chunked transfer decoding, Content-Length check, query string, cookies, Basic auth) into structured JSON, or build a correctly framed raw HTTP message (CRLF line endings, Host and Content-Length) from JSON. Useful for debugging proxies, WAF rules, request smuggling cases and hand-written test fixtures.
  • OpenAPI / Swagger Viewer (Readable Outline)Paste an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document (JSON or YAML) and get a readable outline: servers, auth, every endpoint with parameters, bodies and responses, and the schemas.
  • Swagger 2.0 to OpenAPI 3.0 ConverterConvert a Swagger 2.0 JSON document to OpenAPI 3.0.3: servers, components, request bodies, responses and security schemes.

Developer Playground (1)

  • HTML / CSS / JS Playground (offline sandbox)Write HTML, CSS and JavaScript and see the result live in a sandboxed iframe with a console panel (console.log / warn / error and uncaught errors are captured). The sandbox has no same-origin access and a Content-Security-Policy that blocks all network requests, images from other sites and external scripts, so snippets cannot call out. Download the result as a single .html file.

Audio (21)

  • Audio Converter (any browser-decodable audio to WAV)Decode an audio file your browser understands (MP3, AAC / M4A, OGG, Opus, FLAC, WAV, WebM audio, depending on the browser) and re-encode it as an uncompressed WAV: 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float PCM, optional mono down-mix, resampling to 8-96 kHz, peak normalisation and trimming. Compressed output formats (MP3, AAC) are not available because browsers ship no encoders for them.
  • Audio to FLAC Converter (Lossless)Convert any audio file your browser can play (MP3, M4A, OGG, WAV) to a lossless FLAC file, encoded by hand-written code in your browser. 16 or 24 bit, mono to 8 channels.
  • Audio Joiner with CrossfadeJoin several audio clips into one WAV file, in the order you pick them or sorted by name, with an optional crossfade or a gap of silence between clips.
  • Loudness Normalizer (LUFS Target)Measure integrated loudness in LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770 / EBU R128, K-weighted with gating) and set it to a target such as -16 or -23 LUFS, with peak protection. Writes a WAV file.
  • Audio Speed Changer (Keep or Change Pitch)Speed up or slow down an audio file to a chosen rate. Keep the pitch with a WSOLA time stretch, or change speed and pitch together like a tape. Exports WAV.
  • Pitch Shifter (Semitones, Same Tempo)Raise or lower the pitch of an audio file by semitones and cents without changing its length, using a time stretch plus resampling. Exports WAV.
  • Audio Noise Reducer (Noise Profile)Reduce steady background hiss or hum. Name a stretch of the recording that contains only noise, and spectral subtraction removes that noise profile from the whole file. Exports WAV.
  • Vocal Remover (Center Channel Cancellation)Make a karaoke version of a stereo song by cancelling whatever is identical in the left and right channels, where lead vocals usually sit. A simple phase trick, not AI source separation.
  • BPM Detector for Audio FilesEstimate the tempo of a song from an audio file by analysing onsets and their repeating period. Shows the likely BPM, the half and double values, and a confidence figure.
  • Musical Key Finder for Audio FilesDetect the likely key of a song from an audio file using pitch-class energy and the Krumhansl-Kessler key profiles. Shows the top three keys with Camelot codes for DJ mixing.
  • Audio Fade In and Fade Out EditorAdd a fade-in and a fade-out to an audio file, with a linear, cosine, equal-power or logarithmic curve, and download the result as a WAV file.
  • Silence Remover for AudioCut silent gaps out of a recording, or shorten them. Set the level below which sound counts as silence and the shortest gap to cut, then download the tightened WAV file.
  • Audio Reverser (Play Backwards)Reverse an audio file so it plays backwards, then listen to it and download it as a WAV file.
  • Ringtone Maker (Cut a Clip up to 30 Seconds)Cut a short clip from a song for use as a ringtone or alert sound, with fades and a peak-normalise option, and save it as a WAV file.
  • Audio Equalizer (7-Band, Export WAV)Apply a 7-band equalizer (100 Hz to 8 kHz) to an audio file with presets or your own gains, and download the processed WAV file.
  • Spectrogram Viewer for Audio FilesDraw a spectrogram of an audio file: time across, frequency up, colour for loudness. Choose the window size, a linear or logarithmic frequency axis, and the dynamic range.
  • MP3 Tag Editor (ID3 Tags and Cover Art)Read and edit the ID3 tags of MP3 files: title, artist, album, year, track, genre, comment and cover art. Select the MP3 (and a cover image if you want one). The audio is not re-encoded.
  • Live Audio Spectrum AnalyzerWatch the frequency spectrum of your microphone, or of an audio file as it plays, with the peak frequency and its musical note. Runs locally; nothing is recorded or sent.
  • Drum Machine (16-Step Sequencer)Program a 16-step beat with six built-in drum sounds, play it in a loop with tempo and swing, and export the loop as a WAV file. Sounds are synthesised in your browser.
  • High-Frequency Hearing TestPlay quiet test tones from 8 kHz up to 20 kHz and mark which ones you can hear, to see roughly where your high-frequency hearing ends on your own speakers or headphones.
  • Sleep Noise Player with TimerPlay white, pink or brown noise with a volume control and a sleep timer that fades the sound out and stops it after the minutes you choose. Generated live, no files.

  • Video to GIF ConverterConvert a video segment to an animated GIF in your browser: choose start time, duration, frame rate and width. Frames are grabbed from a <video> element onto a canvas and written with a hand-written GIF89a / LZW encoder using a fixed 256-colour palette with ordered dithering, so file size and colour fidelity are modest (fine for short UI demos; use ffmpeg for photographic quality). Long, large clips use a lot of memory: keep it under about 10 seconds at 480 px.

  • Video Muter: Remove the Audio Track Without Re-encodingRemove the sound from an MP4, MOV or WebM file without touching the picture.
  • Video Metadata Inspector: Codec, Frame Rate, Bitrate and DurationRead container, codecs, resolution, frame rate, bitrate and duration of an MP4, MOV or WebM file without uploading it.
